characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the transformation of δ-ferrite dendrites into lamellar B2 stringer bands after HR

characterization_methods.key_findings: Bright linear shear bands in γ and small IG-B2 particles; fine B2 nucleates at shear bands
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe shear bands in γ and IG-B2 precipitation in the HR state

characterization_methods.key_findings: HR exhibits nearly 6.8% ductility; toughness 0.48 kJ mol⁻¹ (66.5 J cm⁻³)

characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain engineering stress–strain and toughness of the HR sample

characterization_methods.key_findings: Dendrite fraction reduces from 27% (as-cast) to ~19% after HR
characterization_methods.purpose: Estimate dendrite/B2 stringer band fraction after HR

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the multicomponent Fe–10Al–15Mn–0.8C–5Ni system; alloy line at 0.8 wt% C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Outputs are consistent with Ref. [15] for the same alloy composition; predicts δ→B2 order-disorder transition at 1125 °C and eutectoid at 851 °C

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Fine-scale B2 nucleates at shear bands in γ, alleviating lattice strain.

interfaces.phase_evolution: δ-ferrite dendrites transform into lamellar B2 stringer bands during hot rolling between 1050 and 900 °C
interfaces.slip_behavior: Strain localization in the γ matrix via shear band formation during hot deformation

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenization of the ingot at 1150 °C for 2 h in a muffle furnace before hot rolling (parent process of the HR route).

Standard (slow, 1 rpm) hot rolling in a 75-ton rolling mill; nine passes at 1050 °C until finish rolling temperature of 900 °C, then air-cooled. Repeated HR in nine stages causes shape deformation and partial dissolution of dendrites.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: rolling direction (RD); 100 kN Instron 5982 with 10 mm gauge extensometer
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge length 12.5 mm, gauge width 3 mm, thickness 2 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for the HR condition is shown in Figure 5a

phases_present.morphology: matrix, plastically deformed with shear bands
lamellar stringer bands spanning over multiple austenite grains

precipitates.distribution: Fine-scale B2 tends to nucleate at shear bands in the γ matrix

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled γ (austenite) matrix containing lamellar B2 stringer bands transformed from δ-ferrite dendrites; shear bands form in the γ matrix and fine intragranular B2 (IG-B2) precipitates nucleate at those shear bands.

unmapped_findings: The standard (1 rpm) HR sample shows a poor strength–ductility balance (nearly 6.8% ductility and 0.48 kJ mol⁻¹ / 66.5 J cm⁻³ toughness); a modified high-speed HR (10 rpm) route with subsequent annealing raised YS to 1 GPa, elongation to 30% and toughness to 1.72 kJ mol⁻¹ (238 J cm⁻³).
HR is key for refining B2 stringer bands without metal sheet cracking, compared to CR.

Fracture analysis of the standard processed samples shows macrovoid nucleation inside B2 stringer bands, microcrack coalescence and B2 stringer de-cohesion; thicker stringer bands promote crack formation, a mechanism relevant to the premature failure of B2-stringer-containing samples including the sole HR sample.
